subject: Model shortlist, context needs & token-volume sync (onboarding)
body:
From: Nisha Rao <nisha@datasift.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: impl@datasift.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model shortlist + token profile attached — initial traffic signals

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the onboarding kickoff yesterday. Per our internal prep, I'm sharing a quick traffic snapshot and a token-profile worksheet so your team can start the model shortlist and sizing work. Attached: datasift_token_profile.xlsx (sheet: traffic_by_endpoint).

High-level: 
- Monthly active users (MAU): ~85k
- Avg requests/day: ~18k
- Peak concurrent QPS: ~12 (spikey in US/PST hours)
- Request distribution: 70% short prompts (<128 tokens), 25% medium (128–512), 5% long (512–4096) — the long requests are for context-enriched summarization.
- Average output tokens per request: 60
- We expect 15% week-over-week growth for first quarter post-launch.

Context needs: most long requests require a 2–4k token context window (they send customer history + transcript). We are open to proposals that use prefix caching or truncated windowing as long as quality of the long-summary flow remains intact.

Ask: can you confirm which candidate models your engineering team will evaluate and a ballpark per-day token estimate for our current traffic? We want the mutual action plan updated with these numbers so procurement can budget.

cc: impl@datasift.com (engineering lead)

Thanks,
Nisha Rao
Head of Product
DataSift

--- Original attachment: datasift_token_profile.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB) ---

-----
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Nisha Rao <nisha@datasift.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model shortlist + token profile attached — initial traffic signals

Thanks Nisha — this is perfect context. Sharing a short internal note and an initial proposed shortlist (attached) so we can align on cost/latency tradeoffs.

Key clarifying Qs before we finalize estimates:
- For the 5% long requests, is the 2–4k context the total tokens sent (prompt+history) or the model-visible context after any truncation?
- Any SLA constraints on 95th/99th latency for the long-summary flow?
- Are there any PII redaction or on-prem data residency requirements for those long records?

What we'll evaluate initially (high level):
- 7B open transformer (FP16 / int8 variants) — conservative latency, good quality for short/medium.
- 13B dense (quantized) — balanced quality, higher cost but better handling of 2–4k contexts.
- 70B quantized candidate (server-side KV tweaks) — for long-summary alpha tests if we need extra context fidelity.
- A retrieval-augmented pipeline using 2–4k context but with prefix caching for repetitive customer metadata.

Attached: proposed_model_shortlist.csv — includes model id, expected p95 latency (single-token steady-state), rough token cost multiplier, and recommended quantization profiles.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Vivek to produce a token/day and per-hour peak token-rate estimate for the shortlist (including warm-up KV cache effects).
2) Internal engineering sync this week to validate infra tweaks for 4k contexts (GRPC timeouts, batch sizing).
3) We update the mutual action plan with per-token cost bands and a recommended canary plan for the long-flow.

I'll hold a 30-minute slot tomorrow to review if that works for your team.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: proposed_model_shortlist.csv (csv, 8KB) ---

-----
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Nisha Rao <nisha@datasift.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Model shortlist + token profile attached — initial traffic signals

Adding the technical sizing notes below (quick draft) — will post a short PDF with the math and assumptions. Attachment: throughput_estimate.pdf

Vivek's sizing highlights (draft):
- Baseline assumptions: 18k req/day, avg 60 output tokens, request token mix per Nisha. Monthly tokens = ~18k * 60 * 30 ≈ 32.4M output tokens (doesn't include input tokens).
- Input tokens (avg prompt+context): short 40, medium 220, long 1800 (estimate); weighted avg input tokens ≈ 150. Total token units per request ≈ 210. Monthly total tokens (input+output) ≈ 113.4M.
- Peak hour: assume 10% of daily traffic in peak hour => ~1,800 req/hr => ~52 req/sec peak (burst aggregated across microbursts).
- p95 latency targets: short/medium flows target <= 250ms p95 for generation; long-summary target <= 1.2s p95.

Model-specific throughput (approx, single-GPU estimates):
- 7B int8 (A100): ~400 tokens/s per GPU (steady-state inferencing), effective cost multiplier 1x, good for short flows with batching.
- 13B quant (A100): ~180 tokens/s per GPU, cost multiplier ~1.6x, handles 2–4k context with moderate memory pressure.
- 70B q8_0 (SXM): ~55 tokens/s per GPU, cost multiplier ~4–6x depending on sequence length and KV cache usage.

Operational suggestions:
- Use prefix caching for customer metadata; cache hit expected for ~40% of requests (saves ~400 tokens/request on avg).
- Configure tiered routing: short flows -> cheaper 7B pool; medium/long -> 13B pool; long-summary can route to 70B fallback only for high-fidelity requests.
- Canary plan: run 5% traffic to 13B quant for two weeks, measure quality delta on held-out prompts; if >6% improvement in ROUGE/F1 vs 7B, expand to 20%.

Vivek will prepare a short spreadsheet with the per-day token burn for each model candidate (including warm KV cache) and share before the sync.

-- Vivek
Principal Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: throughput_estimate.pdf (pdf, 38KB) ---

From: Nisha Rao <nisha@datasift.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: impl@datasift.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model shortlist + token profile attached — initial traffic signals

Thanks all — this is really helpful. Quick confirmation: the monthly total tokens number (~113M) works for our procurement budget model if the 13B quant path is the primary candidate for medium+long flows and we only route 10% of long-summary traffic to 70B for special cases.

We can take the proposed 30-min sync tomorrow at 11:00 PST. Please send calendar invite and the mutual action plan link so I can attach the estimated numbers for approval.

Also: we'll include a short evaluation prompt set (50 examples) for long-summary quality checks — I'll upload that to the Drive link you shared.

Cheers,
Nisha
Head of Product, DataSift
